papers.title: Cross-species representation learning aligns mouse and human neural dynamics and tracks clinical drug efficacy
papers.summary: The paper presents a dual-rule contrastive learning framework that aligns mouse and human neural dynamics across species while preserving phenotypic separation, recovering conserved sensory-response structure and resolving epilepsy model-patient relationships; it also found that drug-induced movement toward the human-aligned healthy state retrospectively tracked known clinical efficacy across ten model-drug combinations, including a disease-specific detrimental effect.

papers.title: Dual Adaptive Grouped Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition for Physiological Signals.
papers.summary: The paper proposes DA-GMVMD, a method that automatically determines channel groups and mode numbers for grouped multivariate variational mode decomposition of multichannel EEG and ECG signals, using adaptive grouping, adaptive K search, and grouped decomposition. It achieved lower reconstruction error than fixed-parameter GMVMD and baselines on synthetic signals and on CHB-MIT, MODMA, and PTB-XL datasets, while retaining seizure classification information, regional band power, and R-peak timing.

papers.title: Exploiting Phase-Sliding Oscillations for Robust Asynchronous Brain-Computer Interface Control.
papers.summary: The paper reports a phase-sliding oscillation (PSO) phenomenon in SSVEP-based BCIs and proposes a PSO-based asynchronous classification method that achieved 94.2% mean control/noncontrol accuracy offline and reduced command cost per successful trial from 4.30 to 1.14 in online robotic-arm control.

papers.title: The NeuroHab: A Low-Cost, Integrated System for Investigation of Neural Correlates of Behaviors.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Presents NeuroHab, an integrated low-cost (~$1,400) open-source operant conditioning system with solenoid-actuated capacitive lickports, FED3 food reward, conditioned-stimulus modules, and a central controller logging event timestamps at sub-millisecond latency (typically 56-728 μs). The system was deployed in over 50 behavior trials and more than 20 sessions with a Mini two-photon microscope, enabling millisecond-scale alignment of behavior with two-photon imaging and electrophysiology.

papers.title: High-frequency oscillations arise through distinct mechanisms in models of α- synucleinopathy and channelopathy-induced epilepsy.
papers.summary: Compares cortical high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, 250-500 Hz) and interictal spikes in surface EEG from a transgenic α-synucleinopathy model (A53T mice, features of dementia with Lewy bodies) and a channelopathy-induced epilepsy model (Kcna1-/- mice). Both models showed elevated HFOs versus controls, with A53T mice exhibiting more HFOs and spikes, higher HFO frequency, longer duration, and non-REM-sleep predominance, suggesting distinct generation mechanisms and supporting HFOs as a potential biomarker for neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: Toward Personalized Surgeons' Cognitive Workload: A Linear Mixed-Effects Model Analysis of EEG Features.
papers.summary: This study used linear mixed-effects models on EEG data from nine surgical trainees during simulated microvascular anastomosis to show that group-level analysis can mask individual-specific responses to surgical flow disruptions, and introduced a subjectivity index to identify features like Gamma Asymmetry and Mean Power Beta as reliable for personalized cognitive workload monitoring.

papers.title: Topographical Patterns of Slow Wave Activity in Sleep Talking: An Exploratory Polysomnographic Investigation.
papers.summary: This exploratory polysomnographic study compared slow wave activity (SWA) topography across sleep stages in 12 young sleep talkers and 10 matched healthy controls. Sleep talkers showed a stable central SWA increase across sleep stages and a frontopolar decrease primarily in N2 sleep, suggesting local, frequency-specific SWA regulation that may facilitate parasomnia events.

papers.title: The effects of temporal smoothing and interpolation on EEG microstate parameters, syntax, and our view of resting-state brain dynamics
papers.summary: Systematically examines how parametric temporal smoothing and GFP peak interpolation affect EEG microstate sequence parameters in eyes-closed resting-state recordings from 201 healthy subjects. Widening smoothing windows increased microstate duration and decreased occurrence rate, suppressed asymmetry and non-equilibrium dynamics, and strongly altered entropy rate and excess entropy; windows above 30 ms produced a memoryless, aperiodic, time-reversible first-order Markov picture, leading the authors to recommend avoiding intense smoothing.

papers.title: Comparing Maximally Collapsing Metric Learning and Optimized Tunable Q-Wavelet Transform for Schizophrenia Identification Using EEG Signals.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
papers.summary: The study compared a transformer based on Maximally Collapsing Metric Learning (MCML) with optimized Tunable Q-Wavelet Transform (TQWT) for classifying schizophrenia from EEG signals using eight nonlinear features and three classifiers. MCML achieved 100% accuracy with a single electrode channel, outperforming TQWT and other classifiers which reached up to 99.94%.

papers.title: I think, therefore I hit: EEG parameters predict performance in complex cognitive tasks.
papers.summary: The study found that EEG power spectral density parameters from a dual n-back task and the Space Fortress Game could predict complex cognitive task performance in 26 participants, demonstrating the potential of EEG for cross-task performance prediction in aviation.

papers.title: Cross-Subject Localization of Epileptogenic Zone for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy Based on the Causal Brain Network.
papers.summary: The paper presents a method using causal brain network features extracted by full convergent cross mapping (FCCM) from SEEG recordings to localize the epileptogenic zone in drug-resistant epilepsy patients, achieving cross-subject classification with 0.83 accuracy using combined ictal and interictal features, outperforming baseline methods.

papers.title: Variability in Preprocessing and Analysis of the Error-Related Negativity in Adult Response-Conflict Studies: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of 202 adult response-conflict studies from 1995–2025 found highly heterogeneous preprocessing and analysis pipelines for the error-related negativity (ERN), with no two studies using the same workflow and persistent reporting gaps. Analytic decisions showed modest temporal shifts but high overall diversity, sample sizes remained insufficient for typical effects, and preregistrations were extremely rare.

papers.title: Exploratory analysis of electroencephalogram activity preceding nocturnal enuresis episodes using home-based sleep monitoring.
papers.summary: This exploratory study analyzed EEG spectral power immediately before nocturnal enuresis episodes in 18 children using home-based single-channel EEG. Delta-band power was significantly higher on wet nights at 10 and 5 minutes before onset compared to dry nights, suggesting transient sleep deepening preceding enuresis.

papers.title: Daily experiences affect the timing rather than the structure of sleep.
papers.journal: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine
papers.summary: Using a multiday observational study with 1901 nights of mobile EEG and daily diaries, this paper found that daily experiences primarily affect sleep timing rather than sleep structure, with only a few effects on sleep characteristics after accounting for extended wakefulness.

papers.title: Distilling Trial-Level EEG Variability into Participant Representations: Neurophysiologically Constrained Graph Learning in ADHD
papers.summary: Develops a spatiotemporal graph attention network with ERP-informed temporal windows, phase-synchrony graph priors, and trial-to-participant transfer learning to analyze Go/NoGo EEG in children and adolescents with and without ADHD. It finds no reliable spatial attention differences between groups but extracts compact participant-level embeddings that retain diagnostic information beyond convolutional representations and exceed CNN performance.

papers.title: CADENCE: Open-source software for signal conditioning, feature extraction, visualization and analysis of cardiac optical mapping data
papers.summary: Presents CADENCE, an open-source MATLAB-based application for end-to-end processing, analysis, and visualization of cardiac optical mapping data, including denoising, conduction velocity, alternans, and rotor features. Validated against three blinded experts across four species and three tissue preparations, it achieved agreement comparable to inter-observer variability and recovered dominant frequency with a median error of 0.03% across 84/88 paced recordings.

papers.title: Association among white matter lesions, rsEEG rhythms, amyloid tau markers, and cognitive status in mild cognitive impairment patients.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Using an international database of 68 MCI-AD and 44 MCI-noAD patients, this study examined relationships among white matter lesions (WMLs), CSF amyloid-tau markers, resting-state EEG alpha rhythms, and cognition. Greater WMLs were not associated with AD neuropathology, EEG alterations, or worse MMSE in MCI-AD, but higher WMLs were associated with lower MMSE scores in MCI-noAD, suggesting stage-dependent and pathology-specific cerebrovascular-neurodegenerative interactions.

papers.title: Perioperative monitoring in oesophageal atresia and congenital diaphragmatic hernia patients - exploring the impact of diagnosis on neurocardiovascular coupling.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
papers.summary: In an observational cohort of neonates with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) or oesophageal atresia (OA) undergoing surgery, neurocardiovascular coupling was compared using signal interaction graphs from NIRS, aEEG, and clinical monitoring. CDH patients showed significantly stronger intraoperative neurovascular coupling (NVC) than OA patients, and higher sevoflurane dosage was associated with weaker NVC, while other connectivity measures did not differ between groups.

papers.title: Neural latent representation of implicit perceptual decision confidence signatures from brain-wide intracranial EEG
papers.summary: Machine learning applied to brain-wide intracranial EEG without explicit confidence reports identified robust low-dimensional neural latent representations of implicit perceptual decision confidence, with frontal spatiotemporal components distinguishing correctness, difficulty, and speed, and trajectories in a shared subspace improving distinguishability.

papers.title: CoDrag: Coupled Label and Feature Prototype Dragging via Confidence-Aware Estimation for EEG-based Emotion Decoding.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The paper proposes CoDrag, a discriminative regression framework that jointly refines soft-label assignment and latent feature structure via confidence-aware estimation to address feature-label inconsistency in EEG-based emotion recognition. Experiments on SEED-IV, SEED-V, and MPED datasets showed that CoDrag consistently outperformed existing methods in classification accuracy, especially in cross-subject settings, and identified a data-driven emotional prototype structure consistent with subjective emotion distance patterns.

papers.title: The Brain Before the Herd: Pre-Decision EEG Prediction of Herd-Consistent Investment Choices among Bilingual Investors.
papers.summary: In a 2×2×2×2 within-participant EEG experiment with 80 English-Mandarin bilingual investors, Mandarin-language presentation and short-form financial information increased herd-consistent choices under social-fundamental conflict. Pre-decision frontal-midline theta and P300 provided distinct predictive information beyond contextual and participant characteristics, supporting a process-based account of investment conformity.

papers.title: Music-evoked EEG signals for mental health assessment using two- and three-class classification.
papers.summary: This preliminary study used EEG recordings during music and no-music sessions with 48 participants to classify mental fatigue, anxiety, depression, and stress using a deep residual MLP. Binary mental fatigue classification achieved 72.92% accuracy in the music condition vs. 58.33% without music, and multi-output stress classification reached 93.75% accuracy but low AUC due to class imbalance.

papers.title: Integrating resting-state functional connectivity, mismatch negativity, and auditory steady-state responses reveals convergent neurophysiological biomarkers of schizophrenia.
papers.summary: This retrospective secondary analysis of the African Schizophrenia EEG Dataset (153 participants) integrated resting-state functional connectivity, mismatch negativity (MMN), and auditory steady-state responses (ASSR) in a graph attention network. The multimodal framework achieved 91.8% balanced accuracy and 0.96 AUC for classifying schizophrenia, outperforming individual EEG models, with global efficiency, MMN peak amplitude, and ASSR inter-trial phase coherence as top predictive features.

papers.title: A Cortical Stress Signature of Fear-Induced Walking: Mobile Electroencephalography Theta Suppression in Older Women With Fear of Falling.
papers.journal: Psychogeriatrics : the official journal of the Japanese Psychogeriatric Society
papers.summary: In 30 community-dwelling women aged 65 or older, mobile EEG during walking under a naturalistic fear-of-falling stressor showed reduced relative theta power across frontal, temporal, occipital, and sensorimotor regions, with lower frontal and central theta/beta ratios. Theta change was not explained by head movement and gait became more cautious, indicating a cortical stress signature during real walking.

papers.title: A comparative study and analysis of recent EEG-based brain-computer interface approaches and their applications.
papers.summary: This review analyzes recent EEG-based brain-computer interface approaches, covering control signals, feature extraction, classification, performance metrics, and functional connectivity. It compares deep learning models for subject-dependent BCIs and reports ATCNet with the highest accuracy (86.46%) and EEG-TCNet with the lowest (50.69%).

papers.title: High Doses of N-Acetyl-P-Aminophenol Cause Acute Changes in Electroencephalographic and Electrocardiographic Activities in Wistar Rats.
authors: Luiz Gustavo Dos Reis de Freitas
papers.summary: In Wistar rats, a toxic oral dose of N-acetyl-p-aminophenol (1 g/kg) reduced delta, theta, beta, and gamma EEG wave activity while increasing alpha activity, with synchronous reduced cardiac electrical activity. Liver enzymes significantly increased during 12-hour follow-up, indicating early brain and heart electrical changes independent of liver damage.

papers.title: Prognosis of acute symptomatic seizures and impact of prolonged treatment with anti-seizure medication.
papers.summary: In the prospective multicenter PROSE register of 122 adults with first-ever acute symptomatic seizures and structural etiologies, the 3-year cumulative incidence of unprovoked seizures was 14%. Male sex, early epileptiform EEG activity, and latency ≥48 h from underlying condition onset were independent predictors, while anti-seizure medication treatment duration had no apparent effect.

papers.title: Subjective experience of listening to favorite songs and Murottal Al-Qur'an in young adult women: a quantitative EEG case series.
papers.summary: A case series of four young adult women compared alpha-band EEG power during listening to favorite songs and Qur'anic murottal with an eyes-closed baseline. Individual alpha event-related desynchronization/synchronization topography broadly aligned with self-reported mental states (relaxation, visual imagery, concentration) during both conditions, with notable between-subject variability.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation, tolerability, and the Alpha/Theta EEG ratio: a controlled pilot study relevant to emotion regulation.
papers.summary: A controlled pilot study randomized ten healthy female adults to transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) or waitlist control to examine tolerability and EEG Alpha/Theta ratio changes relevant to emotion regulation. The taVNS group completed eight sessions with 100% protocol completion and predominantly grade 1 adverse events; between-group comparisons of change scores favored taVNS for both Alpha/Theta and Theta/Beta ratios, remaining significant after FDR correction, though within-group changes were not significant.

papers.title: A randomized pilot trial of non-flickering 40 Hz light stimulation: EEG activity and cognitive outcomes in cognitively normal older adults.
papers.summary: A randomized, double-blind, active-controlled pilot trial evaluated 4-week non-flickering 40 Hz light stimulation in 33 cognitively normal older adults, with 29 completing the intervention. No significant between-group differences were found in resting-state gamma-band power spectral density or functional connectivity; secondary analyses suggested potential improvements in selected episodic memory measures in the 40 Hz group, and both interventions were well tolerated.

papers.title: Cost-Effective Ultrathin SEBS-Ag Electrodes of Substrate-Regulated Microcracks for Robust Skin Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: The study developed an ultrathin stretchable silver-based electrode by tuning polymer substrate stiffness and polarity, achieving a 7.6 µm electrode with skin-mimetic modulus (1.35 MPa) and low sheet resistance (9.26 Ω/sq). The electrode enabled low-artifact ECG monitoring over 24 h and maintained high signal-to-noise ratio (29.27 dB) during 13 km/h running, outperforming commercial Ag/AgCl electrodes.

papers.title: Temporal profile of serum orexin-A in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a prospective longitudinal study.
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal observational study measured serum orexin-A at 6-12 and 72-96 hours in 41 neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), comparing those treated with therapeutic hypothermia (TH) to those without. Orexin-A trajectories differed significantly: levels were preserved or increased under TH but declined without it, and the change correlated with amplitude-integrated EEG background but not with injury markers.

papers.title: Phase-dependent oscillatory dynamics during needle retention and withdrawal: a comparison of penetrating and non-penetrating acupuncture.
papers.summary: In a 2x2 crossover EEG study with 20 acupuncture-naive participants, verum and sham acupuncture both increased central theta and beta power during needle retention and reduced alpha power post-withdrawal, with the most consistent difference being a weaker alpha reduction for sham compared to verum acupuncture.

papers.title: GIRK Channel Loss of Function Increases Dendritic Excitability in a Mouse Model of GNB1 Encephalopathy.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In a mouse model of GNB1 encephalopathy (Gnb1 p.I80T mutation), hippocampal neurons exhibited simplified dendritic morphology, reduced GABA_B receptor-mediated synaptic inhibition, and increased dendritic excitability with longer calcium spikes, which were reversed by the GIRK channel activator ML297.

papers.title: Serial qEEG as a Neurophysiological Profiling and Treatment Monitoring Tool in dTMS-Treated Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes an 8-year-old male with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who received 40 sessions of qEEG-guided deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (dTMS). Baseline qEEG showed generalized cortical hyperexcitability; serial qEEG monitoring revealed delta reduction and partial resolution of high-beta activity after introducing the H7 coil, and CARS-2 scores decreased from 34 to 20 (41% reduction) alongside reduced anxiety, improved language, and reduced self-injurious behavior.

papers.title: A Structured Framework for Translation of the ACNS Standardized Critical Care EEG Terminology Into Spanish.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: The study developed a consensus-based Spanish translation of the ACNS Critical Care EEG Terminology through a multi-phase methodology involving 45 physicians from Spanish-speaking countries. Consensus was achieved on 25 terms, with final terms such as Generalized Periodic Discharges → Descargas Periódicas Generalizadas (98%) and Lateralized Rhythmic Delta Activity → Actividad Delta Rítmica Lateralizada (100%).

papers.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles
papers.summary: The authors designed and tested 3D-printed hair-anchored EEG electrode attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured hairstyles in 17 healthy adults, comparing them with conventional cap electrodes. Novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance, decreased disconnection rates from 20% to 0.1%, and improved signal quality without reducing comfort.

papers.title: Pragmatic screening for autoimmune-associated epilepsy in drug-resistant epilepsy of unknown etiology in resource-limited settings: A hypothesis-generating study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
authors: Tomásia O de H M Frezatti
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 26 adults with drug-resistant epilepsy of unknown etiology in Brazil, the authors integrated clinical, laboratory, imaging, and EEG findings to assess the feasibility of identifying autoimmune-associated epilepsy in a resource-limited setting, where only one patient could undergo autoantibody testing (confirmed high-titer anti-GAD65). They proposed a pragmatic screening algorithm using accessible markers (e.g., APE2/ACES scores, CSF findings, antinuclear antibodies) to prioritize patients for autoantibody testing when comprehensive testing is unavailable.

papers.title: Noninvasive Intelligent Brain-Metasurface System for Real-Time Electromagnetic Wave Manipulation.
papers.summary: A noninvasive intelligent brain-computer interface was integrated with a reconfigurable metasurface to enable real-time electromagnetic wave manipulation from decoded motor-imagery EEG and EOG commands. The system achieved beam steering, polarization conversion, and radar cross-section reduction, with a peak gain of 18.54-19.29 dBi, 3 dB beamwidth of 12°-15° at +20° steering, and >10 dB RCS reduction across 3.7-3.85 GHz.

papers.title: Neurosyphilis presenting as status epilepticus and hemiplegia diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing: A case report.
papers.summary: A case of neurosyphilis initially misdiagnosed as acute cerebral infarction presented with status epilepticus and hemiplegia. Cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing identified Treponema pallidum, and EEG showed persistent periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges despite anti-syphilitic and antiepileptic therapy.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
